definitions.explanation: A robber or outlaw who operates in mountainous areas, attacking travelers and villages. Used both historically and in fiction.

examples.japanese: {山賊|さんぞく}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{襲|おそ}われる→襲う：01915_osou⟧。
⟦{昔|むかし}→昔：01515_mukashi⟧、⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{峠|とうげ}→峠：02227_touge⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{山賊|さんぞく}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{出没|しゅつぼつ}→出没：28438_shutsubotsu⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧⟦という→という：09577_toiu⟧。
examples.english: They say that bandits used to appear at this mountain pass long ago.

examples.japanese: ⟦{物語|ものがたり}→物語：03634_monogatari⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{主人公|しゅじんこう}→主人公：11404_shujinkou⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{山賊|さんぞく}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{頭領|とうりょう}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧、⟦{富|とみ}→富：12321_tomi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{奪|うば}って→奪う：01895_ubau⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{貧|まず}しい→貧しい：02349_mazushii⟧⟦{人々|ひとびと}→人々：03141_hitobito⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{分|わ}け{与|あた}えた。
examples.english: The protagonist of the story was a bandit chief who stole riches and distributed them to the poor.

notes:
USAGE:
Appears frequently in historical fiction, folk tales, and fantasy settings. The counterpart on the sea is ⟦{海賊|かいぞく}→海賊：13288_kaizoku⟧ (pirate).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {山賊|さんぞく}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{頭領|とうりょう}: bandit chief
- {山賊|さんぞく}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{襲|おそ}われる→襲う：01915_osou⟧: to be attacked by bandits
- {山賊|さんぞく}{焼|や}き: "mountain bandit" grilled chicken (a rustic grilled dish)

CULTURAL NOTE:
{山賊|さんぞく}{焼|や}き is a popular dish in parts of {長野|ながの} and other regions — large pieces of chicken marinated in garlic soy sauce and deep-fried or grilled. The name evokes the rough, hearty eating style of mountain bandits.
